excerpt: Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.

In August 1819, thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter's Field in Manchester, England to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. The crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons, the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion.

A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scenes outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There's a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.

Live at Rockpalast 1999 documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm Mac Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. The show was taped at the height of Dr. John's international popularity and features a setlist of some of his best loved songs.

artist: Mats Edén, Tellef Kvifte, Knut Kvifte Nesheim
excerpt: Mats Edén has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s.

True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa's Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry.
John Alan Urquhart takes you through this cross-cultural landscape.

A little before the end of the last century, a revelatory compilation appeared. From Where I Stand: The Black Experience In Country Music opened a window on something so many didn't even know existed. This expanded 15th anniversary edition marks a good time to look back at the band's mix of Piedmont string band and traditional music.

album: A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking
excerpt: The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakité is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakité, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Hadara.
Vida, the third release by Dani Jané (Spanish guitar, loops, synthesizer, composition), is a lyrical, rhythmic journey.
How do you celebrate fifty years of music? Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino has been at the forefront of the pizzica tradition for half a century.

It's been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she's hardly been idle over the last few years. The long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music.

The acclaimed Swedish female a capella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sound an unlikely mix, but here's a spoiler: it turns out they're pretty much musical best friends.

Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island's best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature.
Polish artist Maria Ka's album Di Mashin (The Machine) explores her Jewish heritage discovered through her family.
John Alan Urquhart introduces us to a unique talent.

The album opens with a striking reinterpretation of singer and Civil Rights activist Abbey Lincoln's Throw It Away, whose message Omicil invokes in his voiceover, an expression of kinship in creative philosophical outlook.

The Visit isn't an album built on compromises. The fourth release from Derksen, a Canadian from the North TallCree Reserve on her father's side, and with a Mennonite lineage from her mother, pushes and cajoles her visions.
